title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization

body: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has become a widely adopted approach for aligning vision-language models (VLMs), yet the security of multimodal preference data remains largely unexplored. Existing preference poisoning attacks either corrupt explicit supervision signals or require visible triggers, making them detectable under human inspection. We introduce DPOison-VL, the first clean preference poisoning attack against VLM-DPO, which manipulates model alignment solely through imperceptible perturbations on a small fraction of training images, while leaving all prompts, responses, and preference annotations semantically intact. We formulate poison construction as a bilevel optimization and derive a gradient alignment surrogate that efficiently steers image perturbations toward the attacker-specified preference. We further introduce a preference displacement score for principled poison selection with provable first-order optimality under a fixed poison budget, and derive a sufficient condition for preference inversion. Extensive experiments across diverse attack tasks, different VLM architectures and scales, and baseline comparisons demonstrate that DPOison-VL achieves up to 98% ASR with only 2% poisoned data and exhibits cross-model transferability, while largely preserving clean accuracy and general utility. Our findings reveal a critical vulnerability in VLM-DPO, where imperceptible image perturbations in preference training data can silently redirect alignment.
summaryZh: 直接偏好优化已被广泛用于多模态大模型的对齐，但其多模态偏好数据的安全性尚未充分探索。本文引入了首个针对VLM-DPO的清洁偏好投毒攻击DPOison-VL，它仅通过对一小部分训练图像施加肉眼不可见的扰动，便能操纵模型对齐，同时保持提示词、响应和偏好标注语义完整。实验表明该方法在仅有2%投毒数据下攻击成功率高达98%，且具备跨模型迁移能力，揭示了偏好数据中的严重安全隐患。
